summary: The document and --parity now state the step that was missing and measure it: a colour-change count is prima facie a LOWER bound, subtracting n8 needs it to be an UPPER bound on the base's traversal, and the licence is that the base cannot step two cells between adjacent columns. base_gaps() (:316-330) measures the spacing over the label-free rows only, which is the right restriction because glyph edges would report one- and two-column spacings that belong to text.
scenario: Pass 2's scenario -- a reader cannot verify that Y8's boundary count may be subtracted rather than only compared -- can no longer occur: the licence is stated in prose in both places and computed by --parity from the image.
evidence: Independently: 152 label-free rows, 916 consecutive-boundary gaps in columns 44..102 of the gold Y8 quad, 910 of them 5 or 6; the six exceptions are gaps of 2, 4 and 7 on rows 52 and 73, identically in all four quads. Worst case 0.5 cells of base index per column against the 1.0 the argument must exclude.

It responds in all three spans, and least densely inside the band (80.8 px/column against 110.7 and 90.5). The claim the control actually needs -- the band is not blind -- is the weaker one, and the document states it correctly at md:264-270.
scenario: A reader runs --control alone, takes the closing sentence over the table two lines above it, and carries 'the Bump env lum offset response is banded 44..102 the way Bump map's Y16 defect is' -- a structural agreement between the two suites that does not exist -- into a model of what the two tests share. remediation: One word: 'including the columns where', not 'in exactly the columns where'.
evidence: The tool's own --control output. Pre-existing since 1f0a5dfd5f; passes 1 and 2 did not flag it.

summary: The flat sub-band's '9..12' Y16 boundary range is pooled over all 168 rows, label rows included, and it is the one per-row count in the remediated paragraph that does not say which side of the label it is on -- against the remediation's own rule at py:80-92 ('every report that quotes a per-column extent or a per-row boundary count has to say which side of it the number is on'). The glyph spans columns 44..90, overlapping 78..90 of the sub-band, so it both adds edges and masks checker boundaries there. Label-free it is 10..11 in every quad; both the 9 and the 12 come from label rows.
scenario: A reader reproducing the sub-band argument restricts to the 150 flat rows, as the surrounding sentence invites, and measures 10..11 against a published 9..12 -- a mismatch with no defect behind it. LOW and not MEDIUM because the direction is conservative: the argument uses the minimum, and including the label rows lowers it from 10 to 9, so no conclusion moves.
remediation: Say '9..12 over all rows, 10..11 outside the label', or restrict the count to label-free rows as base_gaps() already does.
evidence: Per quad, gold Y16 counts in cols 78..102: all rows 10..12 / 9..11 / 10..12 / 9..11; label-free rows 10..11 in all four.
